document_role: implementation intent and acceptance criteria; not proof or qualification evidence

goals.title: Fail-closed exact-current-head formal qualification
goals.summary: Preserve pinned Lean/Mathlib, exact-head isolation, root guardrails, theorem metadata, kernel axiom audit, proof-contract equality, executable/source binding, attestation, and drift detection.
acceptance: Qualification-sensitive source cannot inherit proof status without permitted drift validation.
Unfinished tokens and unexpected axioms fail closed.
Caches accelerate but never substitute for fresh exact-head evidence.

goals.title: Self-validating source and proof sanity checks
goals.summary: CI sanity tools must prove they scanned real inputs and distinguish checker/infrastructure failure from scientific/source failure.
acceptance: Zero-file scans fail closed.
Expected sentinel source is confirmed.
Known-good and deliberately malformed fixtures are exercised.
Distinct failure modes are visible in logs.

goals.title: Repository-contained project memory
goals.summary: A new developer or AI connector must reconstruct goals, architecture, evidence rules, current status, and next priorities without private chat history.
acceptance: AGENTS.md and AI_REPO_MAP.json lead to canonical docs.
Master build specification and machine-readable goal registry remain current.
Historical plans are clearly separated from current status.

goals.title: Full browser scientific canvas
goals.summary: Expose the meaningful CACE Studio workflow through a browser, not merely a thin demo.
acceptance: Drag/drop modules and typed click-to-connect ports work.
Parameter validation, selection, copy/paste, undo/redo, grouping, minimap, zoom, and stale-evidence invalidation are available.
Browser UI consumes canonical core semantics.

goals.title: Browser execution and evidence inspection
goals.summary: Users can run full or selected-upstream graphs and inspect results, assumptions, verification, proof/certificate provenance, and failures.
acceptance: Progress and cooperative pause/resume/cancel are visible.
PASS/FAIL/NOT_RUN/stale states are explicit.
Actual CPU/GPU backend and fallbacks are recorded.

goals.title: Save, replay, export, and print
goals.summary: Versioned .cace experiments and evidence should survive sessions and produce reproducible, readable outputs.
acceptance: Save/load round-trip preserves graph semantics.
Autosave/recovery is available.
Reports, canonical JSON, evidence bundles, data export, and print-friendly views exist.

goals.title: Research Idea objects
goals.summary: Preserve Grow discoveries as editable research notebook objects instead of transient chat.
acceptance: Fields include title, notes, hypotheses, proposed experiment, associated modules, evidence links, and provenance.
Workflow states are Idea -> Testable -> Experimented -> Promising -> Proof Candidate.
Workflow maturity never implies proof.

goals.title: Proposed Experiment -> Build on Canvas
goals.summary: Generate a previewable experiment graph from a Research Idea and mutate the canvas only after approval.
acceptance: Minimal, Balanced, and Exploratory strategies are supported.
Preview includes modules, edges, parameters, assumptions, expected outputs, evidence class, compute estimate, and rationale.
No graph mutation occurs before approval.

goals.title: No-code optional local AI
goals.summary: Users can configure local providers through the GUI while retaining a complete AI-OFF mode.
acceptance: Provider discovery/configuration requires no coding.
AI can explain modules, experiments, rigor, and failures and suggest experiments.
AI output cannot create or promote evidence.

goals.title: Zero-contact local AI sandbox
goals.summary: High-autonomy local AI runs without network/cloud authority and only through bounded approved capabilities.
acceptance: No Internet/cloud credentials/direct host shell access.
Resource limits and auditable action log exist.
Consequential source/canvas mutations can require human approval.

goals.title: Hybrid local neural + LLM assistant
goals.summary: Explore a computationally efficient local AI combining an LLM, lightweight neural component, and validated CACE-derived features/transforms.
acceptance: Any efficiency claim is benchmarked.
Model retrieval uses local project/module/proof metadata.
The model remains outside the trusted verification base.

goals.title: Shared desktop/web/CLI/agent semantics
goals.summary: All interfaces consume the same graph, module, evidence, and claim contracts.
acceptance: No UI maintains an independent scientific truth model.
Core semantics are testable headlessly.
API translations preserve typed assumptions and verification state.

goals.title: Python orchestration with justified C++20 kernels
goals.summary: Keep integration in Python and move expensive stable kernels to C++ behind explicit bindings.
acceptance: Native kernels have independent tests.
Performance claims have benchmarks.
Native speed never changes evidence class.

goals.title: Optional GPU with truthful provenance
goals.summary: GPU acceleration is optional and every run records actual backend/fallback.
acceptance: CPU correctness path remains available.
Fallback is explicit.
CPU/GPU agreement is treated as backend evidence, not proof.

goals.title: Typed plugin/module SDK with isolation
goals.summary: Grow CACE via stable typed modules and progressively stronger isolation for third-party plugins.
acceptance: Manifest compatibility and trust metadata are enforced.
Registration is transactional.
Production target includes capability permissions/process isolation.

goals.title: Certified FEM/PDE end-to-end
goals.summary: Continue mesh, FE spaces, sparse assembly, estimators, certified bounds, adaptivity, higher-order FEM, and goal-oriented estimation after proof gates.
acceptance: Assumptions for each theorem/estimator are explicit.
Numerical certificates link to proof obligations where available.
Conditional continuum results are never presented as unconditional.

goals.title: Graded geometry and Clifford/PGA/CGA foundations
goals.summary: Investigate rotors, spinors, blades, k-cells, and sparse graded representations for useful geometry/science computation.
acceptance: Mappings and invariants are explicit.
Complexity or numerical benefit is measured.
Reusable identities are formally/exactly checked where feasible.

goals.title: Combinatorial-to-geometric low-cost transforms
goals.summary: Study mappings from combinatorial structures/groups into rotors, spinors, blades, cells, or related representations.
acceptance: Domain/codomain, reversibility/information loss, and invariants are specified.
Benchmarks show a meaningful benefit before product promotion.
Failure domains remain documented.

goals.title: Structured serialization and collision-avoidance research
goals.summary: Explore Cantor-style indexing/pairing or other mathematically structured addressing when it measurably improves deterministic IDs, scheduling, or sharding.
acceptance: No mathematical metaphor replaces normal network correctness/security.
Reversibility/collision behavior is proved or exhaustively specified.
Benefit is benchmarked against conventional approaches.

goals.title: Growth/rotation stochastic transform
goals.summary: Explore random generation followed by parameterized exponential-style growth and rotation inspired by e^(i*pi)=-1.
acceptance: State space and transform are defined precisely.
Intended benefit and invariants are specified.
Remains heuristic until validated.

goals.title: Content-addressed Evidence Ledger
goals.summary: Use deterministic artifacts, Merkle identity, signed verifier attestations, append-only transparency records, and optional established external timestamp anchoring.
acceptance: Provenance never creates mathematical proof.
Identity and verifier independence are explicit.
CACE remains fully usable without blockchain/cryptocurrency.

goals.title: Production browser deployment
goals.summary: Host the complete browser-facing Studio behind a stable HTTPS URL, with Oracle Cloud as an accepted target.
acceptance: FastAPI-compatible API and managed process are production-served behind a reverse proxy or equivalent.
Health/readiness and restart policy exist.
App is verified from outside the host.

goals.title: Isolate heavy scientific/proof jobs from web requests
goals.summary: Long Lean/C++/GPU work uses controlled workers/runners rather than being forced into a serverless request lifecycle.
acceptance: Formal qualification runner is isolated from untrusted request execution.
Long jobs expose status/heartbeats.
Thin serverless components, if used, do not become the scientific runtime.

goals.title: Production security and fault tolerance
goals.summary: Harden secrets, sessions, plugins, AI capabilities, parsers, resource limits, recovery, and privileged mutations.
acceptance: No secrets ship in client/repository bundles.
Inputs and uploads are bounded and validated.
Critical boundaries receive fuzz/fault-injection coverage.

goals.title: Curated reproducible demo library
goals.summary: Build a searchable/loadable library of real examples across scientific/mathematical domains and interdisciplinary combinations.
acceptance: Examples declare evidence/maturity.
Historical outputs are not confused with current qualification.
Target scale is approximately 100 high-value demonstrations.

goals.title: Production definition of done
goals.summary: Do not call CACE production-ready until browser workflows, reproducibility, security, deployment, regression evidence, and exposed formal claims are appropriately qualified.
acceptance: Cross-platform/package/web tests pass on the exact release candidate.
Claims are traceable to appropriate evidence.
AI/plugins remain optional and bounded.

goals.title: Coordinate-system visualization palette
goals.summary: Let users switch among Cartesian, triangular, hexagonal, barycentric, lattice, complex-basis, and other coordinate views without changing the underlying mathematics or evidence.
acceptance: Coordinate view state is presentation metadata with its own fingerprint and is excluded from the semantic experiment fingerprint.
Changing a view does not alter theorem hypotheses, numerical inputs, certificates, verification state, or proof status.
Any coordinate transform intended to affect computation is represented as an explicit typed semantic module.
GUI exposes basis/grid/tile/axis/label controls and clearly marks non-semantic modes as VISUALIZATION ONLY.

goals.title: Tiled, complex-base, and fractal coordinate views
goals.summary: Explore hexagonal and other polygonal tilings, Gaussian/Eisenstein-style lattices, experimental i/omega complex-radix views, aperiodic monotile tilings, and hierarchical fractal tile-address coordinate systems.
acceptance: Every view defines a mapping to canonical coordinates and documents ambiguity/non-invertibility.
Hierarchical views can expose recursive tile addresses in addition to canonical coordinates.
Aperiodic/substitution and fractal views remain visualization/research features unless separate mathematical claims are proved.
Novel view renderers report numerical stability and performance limits.

goals.title: Interactive 2D/3D visualization toggle
goals.summary: Provide a GUI button that switches compatible views between 2D and interactive 3D without changing the underlying mathematics or evidence.
acceptance: Users can orbit left/right/up/down by pointer or touch drag.
Zoom, pan, reset/home, fit-to-object, and standard camera presets are available.
Keyboard/button alternatives exist for rotation so dragging is not required.
Camera/view state is presentation metadata and excluded from the semantic experiment fingerprint.
Display-only 3D embeddings are labeled VISUALIZATION ONLY; computational geometry changes require explicit typed semantic modules.

goals.title: Provider-independent run-log retention
goals.summary: Preserve critical proof, CI, deployment, and scientific-run logs outside GitHub using content-addressed durable run bundles and an append-only evidence index.
acceptance: Critical self-hosted runs write complete stdout/stderr, exit codes, manifests, and hashes to durable local storage.
Run bundles are mirrored to OCI Object Storage or another independent durable store.
A canonical manifest binds exact commit, toolchain/environment identity, result, artifacts, and per-file hashes.
An append-only evidence ledger records the manifest digest and storage locations.
GitHub log or artifact disappearance does not destroy the only copy of critical run evidence.
Missing or failed archival is reported explicitly and never changes mathematical proof status.

goals.title: Repository-only build and trust reconstruction
goals.summary: A repository-reading developer or AI must be able to reconstruct the intended webapp, security boundaries, proof rigor, bug-flush architecture, provenance/log retention, deployment shape, and acceptance criteria without private chat history.
acceptance: CACE_AGENT_BOOTSTRAP.json provides a single machine-readable entry point.
BUILD_AND_TRUST_GUIDE.md explains how product, proof, software, security, provenance, and AI assurance dimensions relate.
SECURITY_ARCHITECTURE.md defines trust zones and fail-closed boundaries.
AGENTS.md and AI_REPO_MAP.json route readers through canonical sources rather than historical notes.
The repository distinguishes intended goals, current implementation state, and actually qualified evidence.

goals.title: Zero-egress scientific webapp core
goals.summary: Run the CACE scientific runtime without general Internet access or remote executable/content imports; all network functionality passes through narrow external capability brokers.
acceptance: Scientific worker has no general outbound Internet route.
Frontend loads no third-party runtime scripts/modules/packages or scientific data.
Remote brokers cannot inject Python, JavaScript, Lean source, plugins, packages, archives, shell commands, or arbitrary files.
Only fixed-schema signed/authenticated broker messages cross the sandbox boundary.
Network policy is enforced at OS/process/container level, not only by UI convention.

goals.title: Invite-only network shared canvas
goals.summary: Allow users to invite viewer/editor collaborators into an encrypted shared CACE canvas without giving the scientific sandbox general network authority.
acceptance: GUI provides Collaborate/Invite with link and/or QR invitation.
Typed canvas operations synchronize through a separate broker/relay.
Room capabilities are authenticated, revocable, role-scoped, replay-protected, size/rate limited, and end-to-end encrypted where practical.
Collaboration cannot install code/plugins or directly promote evidence.
Local work continues safely when network connectivity is lost.

goals.title: Sandbox every local CACE instance
goals.summary: Run local scientific instances with OS-enforced isolation, least privilege, resource quotas, read-only runtime, separate workspace, and no credentials or arbitrary shell/network authority.
acceptance: Instance uses an unprivileged identity and no-new-privileges policy.
Program/runtime is read-only and writable workspace is isolated.
CPU/RAM/process/disk/time limits are enforceable.
No cloud credentials, Docker socket, package-manager authority, or arbitrary shell are exposed.
Local AI receives an equal or stricter sandbox.

goals.title: Day/week/month/year Monero research passes
goals.summary: When standard compute time is exhausted, show a Monero payment QR and allow 1-day, 1-week, 1-month, or 1-year signed research passes that support R&D and compute costs.
acceptance: License expiry blocks new compute without deleting saved work or changing evidence truth.
Payment QR shows plan, duration, price, quoted XMR amount, address/subaddress, and activation status.
Production unlock requires a signed capability token from a payment verifier; localStorage or an arbitrary transaction hash cannot unlock.
Scientific sandbox contains only the license verification public key, never wallet spend keys or license-signing private keys.
USD policy price and XMR conversion are separated so cryptocurrency volatility does not silently change product economics.

goals.title: Professional scientific-software pricing policy
goals.summary: Use tiered Basic, Researcher, and Enterprise pricing appropriate to intended use while keeping commercial policy separate from mathematical qualification.
acceptance: Basic is the lowest-price pass tier and grants a one-time 24-hour introductory entitlement.
Researcher is the middle-price pass tier and grants a one-time 48-hour introductory entitlement.
Enterprise is the highest-price tier and is required for commercial/business engineering or scientific use.

Initial target pricing is Basic $4.99/day, $14.99/week, $39/month, $199/year; Researcher $14.99/day, $49/week, $149/month, $999/year; Enterprise $99/day, $399/week, $1,499/month, $9,999/year per named seat.
Pricing lives in a signed/configurable commercial policy rather than qualification-sensitive mathematical source.
Remote cloud/GPU/proof compute is capped, fair-use, queued, or metered separately from local application time.

goals.title: Account login with hardened password storage
goals.summary: Provide durable user accounts without placing end-user authentication secrets on scientific or proof runners.
acceptance: Passwords are never stored in plaintext or reversible form.
Password verifiers use Argon2id with unique salts and versioned/tunable parameters.
Credential submission uses authenticated encrypted transport.
Proof/scientific runners receive no plaintext passwords, password hashes, reset tokens, or general account-database credentials.
Email verification, password reset, session revocation, and audit events are supported.

goals.title: Durable entitlement and payment ledger
goals.summary: Record free trials, Monero invoices/payment observations, granted passes, revocations, and delivery events in an auditable append-only commercial trail.
acceptance: Basic first-time free allowance is recorded as one 24-hour entitlement.
Researcher first-time free allowance is recorded as one 48-hour entitlement.
Every paid entitlement references a durable invoice/payment event trail.
Browser/local client state alone cannot create or extend entitlements.
Scientific runtime receives only a signed entitlement token.

goals.title: Enterprise full-rigor proof purchase workflow
goals.summary: Allow verified Enterprise users to request a customer-specific rigorous proof package, but require the requested result to pass the normal CACE qualification pipeline before the customer is asked to sign/pay.
acceptance: Proof order freezes and hashes the relevant canvas, assumptions, requested result, and software/proof versions.
Customer first receives a contingent quote; bespoke proof qualification then occurs before signature/payment.
The requested result must pass kernel, axiom, theorem-metadata, provenance/attestation, and artifact-integrity gates before status becomes PROOF_READY_FOR_SALE.
If proof-ready qualification fails, CACE revises scope/quote or declines the order rather than selling an unqualified result.
After proof-ready status, the exact qualified result is bound into the SOW/IP schedule, then signature/payment occurs.
Customer-facing PDF includes the agreed customer-specific derivation, limitations, and provenance while excluding protected CACE Background IP.
PDF/manifests are hashed and delivery is audit logged.

goals.title: Separate CACE Background IP from customer Foreground deliverables
goals.summary: Contracts retain CACE reusable/proprietary theorem infrastructure while assigning or licensing agreed customer-specific deliverables to the Enterprise customer to the extent legally transferable.
acceptance: Contracts define Background IP, Foreground IP, customer data, generic improvements, and excluded reusable CACE technology.
CACE proprietary base theorems, internal lemmas, proof strategies, reusable libraries, and tooling remain Background IP unless expressly sold separately.
Customer-specific protectable deliverables can transfer after full payment according to the signed IP schedule.
Marketing does not promise exclusive copyright or patent ownership in mathematical facts/formulas where statutory law does not provide such rights.

Reasonable secrecy measures include private repositories, least-privilege access, MFA for privileged accounts, encryption, disclosure classification, audit logs, confidentiality agreements, and mandatory customer-export review.
Customer PDFs disclose no more reusable proprietary theorem machinery than the contract requires.

goals.title: Separate proof runner from account, contract, and email credentials
goals.summary: Proof runners publish signed artifacts/results through a narrow internal channel; account, payment, contract, database, and outbound-email functions run in separate services.
acceptance: Proof runner cannot query user/password tables.
Proof runner has no outbound mail credential.
Proof runner has no Monero spend key or customer payment credentials.
Mail/document services verify contract/payment/proof status before customer delivery.
A PDF hash mismatch, unsigned result, or incomplete contract/payment gate blocks delivery.

goals.title: Continuous reasonable-measures protection for proprietary theorem corpus
goals.summary: Protect CACE proprietary base theorems and reusable proof machinery with concrete technical, contractual, and operational secrecy controls so customer deliverables can be rigorous without exposing the underlying trade-secret corpus.
acceptance: Proprietary theorem repositories remain private and are separated from customer/public interfaces.
Theorem files/modules carry disclosure classifications and customer export tools exclude trade-secret source by default.
Privileged access uses least privilege, MFA/passkeys, periodic access review, prompt offboarding, and temporary elevation where practical.
Sensitive repositories, backups, and proof artifacts are encrypted at rest and transferred only over authenticated encrypted channels.
Access/export of designated trade-secret material is audit logged and unusual bulk export patterns can be investigated.
Employees, contractors, reviewers, and relevant vendors are bound by appropriate confidentiality/IP obligations.
Every enterprise proof passes a pre-sale deliverability review and a final pre-delivery disclosure review.
Evidence that secrecy measures were actually used is retained over time.

goals.title: Tiered GPU/CUDA and CPU multithread controls
goals.summary: Expose explicit execution-backend controls without changing mathematical semantics: GPU acceleration for all tiers, CPU multithreading included for Researcher/Enterprise, and a permanent $15 Basic multithread unlock.
acceptance: Basic, Researcher, and Enterprise all have a GPU Acceleration ON/OFF control.
CUDA is exposed only when a compatible NVIDIA CUDA backend is detected; generic GPU support must not be mislabeled as CUDA.
Researcher and Enterprise include a Multithread CPU ON/OFF control.
Basic is single-threaded by default and can buy feature.cpu_multithread.basic.perpetual.v1 once for $15.
The Basic multithread purchase is a durable account entitlement and is recorded in the payment/audit ledger.
Every numerical run records requested/actual backend, thread count, CUDA/device identity where applicable, and fallback reason.
Acceleration settings never promote proof status or bypass verification gates.

goals.title: Fail-closed source-secrecy release gates
goals.summary: Protect proprietary CACE implementation through classification, client dependency boundaries, sealed native components, inexpensive authenticated encryption at rest, CPU/GPU data minimization, final-artifact scanning, and adversarial release testing.
acceptance: Crown-jewel theorem/proof machinery remains off customer hardware whenever local execution does not require it.
Browser production bundles contain no proprietary scientific algorithm source, source maps, private theorem source, or remotely loaded executable code.
Protected local implementation migrates away from plain Python source toward a narrow compiled native ABI where secrecy justifies it.
Sensitive local assets use vetted authenticated encryption with keys kept out of binaries and unwrapped through OS-backed key storage where available.
GPU/CUDA interfaces receive only declared numeric buffers/opaque operation IDs and never theorem source, proof scripts, signing keys, or account secrets.
Final customer artifacts pass security/release_secrecy_policy.json through scripts/check_release_secrecy.py before publication.
Leakage defects trigger the same reproduce/root-cause/sweep/permanent-guard loop used by the bug-flush architecture.
Security documentation explicitly states that local execution on adversarial hardware cannot be made impossible to reverse engineer.

goals.title: Minimal CPU/GPU plaintext exposure
goals.summary: Keep proprietary code/text out of accelerator data paths and minimize the lifetime/scope of decrypted protected assets without adding unnecessary encryption overhead to hot numerical loops.
acceptance: CPU/GPU transfer schemas declare the exact allowed buffer types, shapes, classifications, and maximum sizes.
GPU memory never receives proprietary theorem/source text, proof scripts, signing keys, license secrets, or unrelated internal metadata.
Protected assets decrypt on demand and are not serialized to plaintext temporary files.
Native sensitive buffers are best-effort wiped after use where practical; Python strings are not treated as securely erasable.
Encryption is used at rest and at trust boundaries rather than indiscriminately encrypting ordinary hot-loop numerical buffers.
Release/adversarial tests inspect binary strings, symbols, browser bundles, GPU metadata, and normal accelerator buffers for accidental leakage.

goals.title: Minimize user-triggered proof jobs through batched qualification
goals.summary: Accumulate compatible theorem work behind quarantine and cheap CI, then compile multiple quarantined Lean modules in one manual exact-pin batch rather than requiring one user dispatch per theorem sub-batch.
acceptance: Heavy formal-proof workflows remain manual-only and serialized on cace-oci-a1.
A batched exact-pin workflow accepts multiple explicit quarantined CACEFormal/*.lean targets and validates every target as quarantined-standalone.
The batch compiles all requested targets and reports the complete failure frontier before exiting.
The batch emits exact-head, target-manifest, toolchain, Mathlib, per-target status, logs, and content-addressed evidence.
Cheap source-sanity/collaboration tests run automatically as theorem work accumulates.
Passing a batched preflight does not promote modules or create qualification evidence.
After a successful batch, promotion is atomic and final exact-head canonical qualification remains required.
Agents should group user-required Actions dispatches whenever doing so does not weaken proof rigor.

goals.title: Cross-chat continuity and redundant idea handoff
goals.summary: Every substantive CACE chat should recover the durable handoff, preserve new meritorious ideas, refresh the live frontier, and mirror the continuity bundle outside GitHub so a new chat can continue without reconstructing private history.
acceptance: Repository contains a self-contained cross-chat handoff and append-only chat-derived idea ledger.
ChatGPT Library mirrors exist under /CACE CONTINUITY/ when Library access is available.
New chats re-query live GitHub/CI state rather than trusting stale snapshot status.
Meritorious ideas are deduplicated into the idea ledger/goal registry without changing evidence status.
Continuity updates avoid qualification-sensitive source changes and never promote proof claims.

goals.title: Reasoning-first local AI curriculum and anti-memorization evaluation
goals.summary: Train compact local AI on reusable typed operations, compositions, invariants and counterfactual structure rather than answer memorization; evaluate with procedurally generated paired interventions, symmetry/invariance transforms, inverse problems and held-out compositions.
acceptance: Training/eval tasks are procedurally generated with held-out structural templates and compositions.
Canonical and load-bearing perturbed pairs are evaluated together; irrelevant perturbations test invariance.
Model can emit an externally executable/type-checkable operator program without requiring hidden chain-of-thought disclosure.
Evaluation reports pair correctness, necessary-flip sensitivity, invariance, isomorphism transfer, composition holdout and distractor robustness.
AI output and reasoning metrics never promote formal or scientific verification state.
Implementation is independently designed from public/general concepts and all third-party code/data has explicit compatible licensing.
Reasoning curricula should exploit exact combinatorics, symmetry groups and group actions when they measurably reduce equivalent search states or improve compositional transfer.
goals.inspiration: Sophonic-AI-inspired at the high-level idea level; independently implemented by CACE with no implied affiliation or use of non-public methods.

goals.title: Conway-inspired canvas and local-AI heartbeat field
goals.summary: Give each semantic canvas item a deterministic cellular heartbeat state and expose graph/heartbeat deltas to the local AI for attention, coordination and visualization without granting evidence authority.
acceptance: Each canvas node has typed heartbeat states such as dormant, ready, active, waiting, blocked, stale, verifying, verified, failed and research-interest.
Heartbeat rules are deterministic, dependency-aware and versioned.
AI attention/research states are technically unable to set VERIFIED/PASS.
Semantic hash changes propagate stale state through hard dependencies.
Canvas overlay visualizes heartbeat activity separately from scientific evidence.
Heartbeat delta can be included in local-AI context packets without requiring full-canvas rereads.
A typed agent perception packet can carry compact residual/convergence/blocker/resource/evidence deltas so local AI can follow the live experiment without rereading the full canvas.

goals.title: Typed atoms, molecules, and safe home-lab chemistry
goals.summary: Add typed atom/bond/molecule objects and a fail-closed Safe Home Lab mode limited to low-risk educational household chemistry.
acceptance: Atoms, bonds, and molecules have typed serializable scientific-object schemas.
Safe Home Lab uses an explicit low-risk whitelist and rejects unsupported hazardous procedures.
Chemistry canvas objects can connect through typed ports without conflating visualization with evidence.
Outputs retain provenance, limitations, and evidence class.

goals.title: License-safe protein structure import and low-cost fold search
goals.summary: Support supplied protein sequences and imported AlphaFold-compatible structures, plus a deterministic low-cost coarse folding/energy search labeled as lowest energy found rather than proven global minimum.
acceptance: AlphaFold-compatible imports preserve source/license/attribution metadata.
AlphaFold 3 weights are not bundled without separate terms review.
Fold search is deterministic under a fixed seed and reports energy trace plus limitations.
No UI/report language claims a proven global thermodynamic minimum or clinical validity.

CACE can resolve a user-supplied UniProt accession through the current public AlphaFold DB prediction API, follow only allowlisted HTTPS AlphaFold structure URLs, and preserve CC-BY-4.0 attribution plus content hashes.

The Protein Playground provides a one-click AlphaFold DB → Canvas + Fetch path; after selected-node execution, the typed structure is discoverable by the existing residue/source-node heartbeat Play adapter.

goals.title: Mathematical materials candidate screening
goals.summary: Generate and rank material hypotheses from composition/structure descriptors and explicit property targets while distinguishing heuristic, surrogate, physics-based, database, and measured evidence.
acceptance: Candidate scoring is reproducible and mathematically inspectable.
Each predicted property carries source/model/uncertainty metadata.
Material search is computational screening only and does not silently emit synthesis instructions.
Candidates can become Research Ideas and Proposed Experiments.

goals.title: Typed draggable particle, field, and theoretical physics objects
goals.summary: Add draggable physics objects for Standard Model entities and explicitly theoretical constructs such as strings/worldsheets with correct evidence labeling.
acceptance: Established and theoretical objects are technically distinguishable.
Quark renderers preserve a confinement caveat.
Theoretical string/brane objects cannot be presented as experimentally established particles.
Objects interoperate with transform/geometry modules through typed ports.

goals.title: Open Problems Toolkit with canvas import and AI Play
goals.summary: Provide a source-backed, date-stamped GUI catalog of important open scientific/mathematical problems that can be imported as typed canvas objects and explored with heartbeat-guided local AI without promoting AI/numerical output to proof.
acceptance: Problem entries carry authority, source URL, status and last-verified date.
V1 ships a verified Millennium Prize snapshot and supports strict custom catalog JSON.
Users can search/filter, import a problem to the canvas, and press Play.
Play uses non-authoritative heartbeat/local-AI context and cannot create PASS/VERIFIED evidence.
Solved historical problems are visibly distinguished but can still be studied as methodological examples.
Scientific runtime remains offline-first; catalog URLs are metadata rather than implicit network fetches.

goals.title: Conway heartbeat spare-compute economy
goals.summary: Turn the non-evidentiary canvas heartbeat into an internal compute-credit game that harvests spare CPU/GPU headroom, budgets exploratory work, and learns scheduling efficiency from externally measured outcomes without monetary value or verification authority.
acceptance: Credits have no monetary/crypto value and cannot alter evidence or proof status.
Credits are minted only from bounded resource-headroom measurements and capped per node/treasury.
Allocation is deterministic for the same heartbeat/bids/resource snapshot.
AI self-reported success cannot mint rewards; only scheduler/executor measurements may update efficiency statistics.
Research tasks can spend credits while user/verification-critical work can bypass or preempt the game.

goals.title: Default-off superintelligence-class capability gate
goals.summary: Add an explicit GUI gate that denies providers/manifests classified as superintelligence-class unless the user opts in, while independently retaining sandbox, network, self-modification, evidence, and resource controls.
acceptance: Default setting is OFF.
OFF rejects superintelligence-class provider manifests before inference.
ON is permission to admit that capability tier, not a claim that a model is or is not superintelligent.
Network, self-modification, shell/tool authority, evidence mutation, and compute budgets remain separate fail-closed capabilities.
Current loopback-only local providers remain bounded by the existing local-provider security model.

goals.title: Immutable one-way deep-layer matrix observers
goals.summary: For locally instrumentable open models, copy hidden-layer activation matrices through a host-controlled one-way broker into two or more isolated observer containers so the AI cannot alter observer policy or receive an observer feedback channel.
acceptance: Observer configuration/manifests are host-owned and content-addressed.
Model-to-observer flow is one-way; observer containers expose no return/control channel to the model.
At least two observer replicas can independently hash/encode the same layer-step matrices.
Weights and observer runtime are read-only where practical; observer archives are append-only/content-addressed.
Full hidden-layer capture is optional and resource-bounded; compact sketches/hashes are supported when full capture is too costly.
Feature is only advertised for inference engines that actually expose layer activations.

goals.title: Math Coin burn-to-compute heartbeat economy
goals.summary: Research a fixed-supply Math Coin compute-right token for the Conway heartbeat economic city: 500 billion genesis supply, no mining or block rewards, most supply locked in a long-horizon vault, discrete decade release tranches, and irrevocable burn when metered computation is successfully consumed.
acceptance: Genesis maximum supply is exactly 500,000,000,000 MATH and ordinary runtime operation cannot mint above that cap.
There is no proof-of-work/proof-of-stake mining reward or per-block token issuance; new circulating supply comes only from a precommitted vault-release schedule.

More than half of genesis supply begins in a time-locked vault and releases occur only as discrete all-at-once tranches at 10-year boundaries; tranche quantities are explicit constitutional parameters rather than AI-controlled values.
Compute purchase uses reserve/escrow first and burns MATH only after host-measured compute consumption settles; failed/cancelled work cannot fabricate a burn receipt.
Burn receipts bind task identity, measured compute units, price rule, payer wallet/capability, provider, exact token amount, transaction identity, and immutable audit hash.
Internal CACE compute credits remain non-monetary scheduler state and are never silently interchangeable with MATH.

AI agents never receive raw wallet private keys; real-crypto/MATH trading passes through a separately permissioned broker with per-agent budgets, allowlists, exposure limits, audit logs, and human-configurable shutdown.
Compute providers can be compensated through a separate settlement leg even though the buyer's MATH compute-right is burned.
The Conway heartbeat economic-city visualization cannot promote scientific evidence, theorem status, or verification state.
Any production exchange against real cryptocurrency requires a separate security, market-integrity, accounting, and jurisdiction-specific compliance review.

goals.title: Gemini-first AI builder contract with evidence isolation
goals.summary: Use Gemini AI Code Studio as the primary implementation environment while enforcing one repository-visible builder contract that keeps AI outside proof/evidence authority and preserves CACE trust boundaries.
acceptance: CACE_AI_BUILDER_CONTRACT.md is discoverable from agent/bootstrap navigation.
All AI builders classify changes by trust impact before implementation.
AI-generated code, tests, theorem sketches, and metadata can never independently create formal PASS.
Proof-sensitive changes preserve quarantine, Exact-Pin, audited-root, canonical qualification, and drift rules.
CACE remains fully usable with AI disabled.

goals.title: Concrete runtime-to-formal P1/RT0 and continuum linkage
goals.summary: Build an auditable fail-closed chain from canonical runtime mesh/P1/RT0 packets to exact Lean objects, discrete theorem instantiation, and eventually bounded-box H1/H(div)/volumePairing continuum hypotheses.
acceptance: docs/proofs/SOURCE_TO_FORMAL_LINKAGE_SPEC.md defines FSL-0 through FSL-13.
Runtime packet identity is deterministic and content-addressed.
P1/RT0 coefficients and certified mesh geometry are bound exactly or remain non-formal.
Discrete exact theorem instantiation is kept separate from continuum graph-space membership.
H1/H(div) membership, finite-sum to volumePairing equality, trace cancellation, and cross-term identification require explicit Lean theorems.
Missing or stale bindings remain unresolved/NOT_RUN.
Canonical proof contract and exact-current-head qualification remain mandatory for formal promotion.

goals.title: CACE Rigorous Math Kernel v1
goals.summary: Build a canonical C++ mathematical substrate for exact rationals, sparse linear algebra, polynomial/affine algebra, geometry, exterior/graded primitives, calculus operators, piecewise fields, norms, and deterministic proof-linkage packets, with Python as thin orchestration.
acceptance: Canonical exact mathematical objects are deterministic, typed, content-addressed, and fail closed on malformed/overflow conditions.
Load-bearing algorithms are implemented once in C++ and not duplicated in Python or browser code.
Exact, interval, symbolic, numerical, reviewed, and formally connected evidence modes remain distinct.
Runtime objects intended for formal use have explicit source-to-formal binding hooks compatible with FSL obligations.

goals.title: Broad proof-backed mathematical toolbox
goals.summary: Expose a large canonical module library across algebra, linear algebra, calculus, geometry, combinatorics, analysis, FEM/variational mathematics, graph-space obligations, and transforms, reusing qualified Lean results where explicit runtime bindings exist.
acceptance: Production math tools use semantic canonical module IDs instead of proliferating historical version wrappers.
Every module exposes assumptions, limitations, evidence badges, and verifier behavior.
Existing Lean theorem families are mapped to useful runtime tools without inferring FORMAL status from file existence.
Reviewed mathematics remains REVIEWED until a real formal bridge and current qualification exist.

goals.title: Full-featured composable science modules
goals.summary: Systematically upgrade science modules into typed, unit-aware, verifiable, reusable building blocks sharing canonical math/geometry/field/material/solution/evidence objects so modules from the same or different domains link naturally on the canvas.
acceptance: Each production-intended science module defines typed ports, units, assumptions, execution, verification, reproducibility metadata, limitations, and interoperable shared object types.
Core workflows can be assembled by typed connections rather than UI special-casing module-name pairs.
Important outputs have an appropriate exact, interval, invariant, residual, convergence, reference, cross-method, or formal verification path when feasible.
Historical modules migrate through compatibility adapters instead of abrupt deletion.
A science domain is production-complete only after representative end-to-end module chains, input guidance, validation, evidence, Help/examples and failure handling pass together.

goals.title: Integrated module Help pages and runnable example library
goals.summary: Give every production-intended math/science module structured Help content, worked examples, Canvas-loadable experiments, connection suggestions, evidence explanations, and troubleshooting.
acceptance: Help answers purpose, theory/equations, inputs/outputs, units, assumptions, evidence strength, limitations, references, and failure causes.
Each production-intended module has a minimal example and realistic example; important modules also have composition and failure examples.
Examples are executable/versioned/tested and can be added directly to Canvas.
Long-term curated example library grows toward roughly 100 high-value demonstrations without confusing historical outputs with current evidence.

goals.title: Bounded AI context pack for Gemini and Antigravity
goals.summary: Guarantee coding agents see the complete A-I implementation program, durable goals and idea ledger without exceeding Gemini's observed ~1000-file ingestion limit.
acceptance: AI_CONTEXT/00_START_HERE.md is reachable from AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md and CACE_AGENT_BOOTSTRAP.json.
Planned context pulls are capped at 800 files and fail closed on truncation/discard.
Tier 0 always includes GOAL_REGISTRY and CHAT_IDEA_LEDGER so deferred ideas are not lost.
Task source is loaded in deterministic shards rather than whole-repository bulk pulls.

goals.title: Provider-independent local agent runtime with heartbeat recovery
goals.summary: Build CACE-owned local agentic AI with zero-contact mode, typed tools, leases, checkpoints, semantic canvas heartbeats and strict evidence isolation.
acceptance: Local/Zero Contact mode requires no cloud/network dependency.
Agent liveness, progress, checkpoint and verification states remain distinct.
Heartbeat/checkpoint protocol supports monotonic sequencing, lease expiry and recovery.
AI/heartbeat state cannot create PASS, VERIFIED, FORMAL or proof-ledger promotion.
The local agent may propose/build reusable tools through the rigorous contribution pipeline, but accepted capability and evidence promotion remain independently governed.

goals.title: AI-built C++ tools with formalization and proof-ready handoff
goals.summary: Allow Gemini, Antigravity and local agents to improve CACE by implementing canonical C++ tools, tests, exact/certified checkers, Lean proof attempts and runtime-to-formal bindings, with a machine-readable handoff whenever formal closure remains.
acceptance: Gemini has an explicit Rigorous Tool Builder mode in repository-visible instructions.
New load-bearing math/science algorithms are implemented in C++ rather than duplicated in browser code.
AI may write Lean theorem statements/proofs but cannot self-promote FORMAL/PASS.
Incomplete formal work can be preserved as a validated cace-ai-tool-submission-v1 packet with unresolved obligations and next gate.
Accepted tools follow the ordinary CACE engineering/formal promotion ladder before production/formal presentation.

goals.title: Research-assistant-first post-account onboarding and daily workspace
goals.summary: After account creation, greet the user with a local Research Assistant chat that can accept a natural-language experiment, recommend real demos relevant to the user's field, show full CACE capabilities, or resume recent work; then transition continuously into the scientific canvas with the assistant remaining available.
acceptance: Newly entitled users land on a Research Assistant welcome experience instead of an unexplained empty canvas.
The assistant offers Describe an experiment, Show demos for my field, Explore full capabilities, and Open recent work when available.
Demo recommendations are grounded in structured real demo/module metadata rather than fabricated availability.
Natural-language intent can produce a previewable typed experiment graph with Minimal/Balanced/Exploratory variants and Build on Canvas.
The welcome chat persists as the Studio Research Assistant after the canvas opens.
CACE presents itself as a VRE/Verified Research Environment while exposing the actual evidence class of every result rather than implying all modules are formally verified.

Preferred product message is 'Explore rigorous math with AI that learns geometric reasoning,' with learning defined through local research memory, accepted tools, geometric representations, and validated workflows rather than AI-generated truth.
Returning users can use the assistant as a daily research workspace companion with recent experiments, Research Ideas, stale/blocked work, and suggested next steps.
Local/Zero Contact mode supports the experience without required cloud AI, and a no-AI fallback remains fully usable.
Heartbeat/perception gives the assistant contextual awareness of the running experiment without any evidence authority.

goals.title: Experiment-to-proof discovery loop
goals.summary: Running experiments should surface theorem matches, exact identities, invariants and proof candidates; CACE should connect applicable qualified theorems or create explicit proof obligations and feed successfully formalized reusable mathematics back into the toolbox.
acceptance: Suitable runtime results can emit typed non-authoritative ProofOpportunity records linked to exact experiment/node semantic hashes.
Existing theorem matching checks hypotheses, representation identity and source-to-formal requirements rather than text similarity alone.
Unmatched opportunities become persistent Proof Candidate Research Ideas with assumptions, counterexample history and unresolved obligations.
Numerical/empirical patterns never auto-promote to formal proof; AI proof attempts enter quarantine and ordinary proof gates.
Qualified reusable results can be promoted through normal engineering review into canonical tools, Help/examples and AI ReasoningOperators.

goals.title: End-to-end production completeness gate
goals.summary: No feature, module or scientific domain is considered production-grade unless its complete user workflow works together: typed inputs, connections, execution, validation, evidence, Help, examples, persistence, failure handling and UI/API/agent integration.
acceptance: Every advertised production module has stable typed inputs/outputs, assumptions, validation, verification behavior, structured Help and runnable examples.
Compatible modules connect through canonical shared object types without pair-specific UI hacks.
End-to-end tests exercise representative cross-module workflows, not only isolated units.
Complex-input modules provide guided input/wizard support where needed.
Missing, stale, NOT_RUN and failure states remain visible and understandable.
A domain cannot be marketed as production-grade while required modules or connections are placeholders, broken, duplicated or browser-only.

goals.title: Typed equation and data wizard with high-quality math rendering
goals.summary: Complex mathematical/scientific inputs should be created through a guided typed wizard with symbol definitions, units/domains, validation, structured data import and readable rendered equations that round-trip through canonical CACE semantics.
acceptance: Equation input parses to a canonical typed AST and renders high-quality mathematics; LaTeX is an export/presentation format rather than the semantic source of truth.
Wizard steps collect variables, domains, units, assumptions, boundary/initial conditions and module-specific requirements.
Undefined symbols, type/shape/unit/domain errors and missing required conditions are caught before expensive execution where feasible.
Data import previews mappings and never silently discards or reinterprets columns.
Wizard output is editable, serializable and identical in semantics across GUI/API/CLI/agent paths.
Research Assistant can conversationally populate wizard fields while deterministic validation remains authoritative.

goals.title: Combinatorial and group-action reasoning acceleration
goals.summary: Expand exact combinatorics, finite groups and group-action tools and integrate them with geometric representations/operator memory so the Local AI can canonicalize symmetry-equivalent states, compose reusable transformations and reduce reasoning/search cost.
acceptance: Canonical tools cover permutations, combinations, finite explicit groups, group actions, orbits/stabilizers, canonical representatives and small-group Cayley structures where tractable.
Group/combinatorial objects can act on supported vectors, frames, cells, blades, graphs and other typed geometry through explicit checked mappings.
Accepted tools expose ReasoningOperator metadata including preconditions, invariants, inverses/composition and failure domains.
Efficiency improvements are benchmarked against suitable non-group/operator baselines rather than assumed.
Exact/formal status follows the ordinary evidence pipeline; representational compression cannot weaken rigor.
goals.inspiration: Part of the Sophonic-AI-inspired geometric-reasoning/training direction; exact combinatorics/group-action implementation and evaluation remain independently designed in CACE.
